items.html: Claudication history. The history asks where the pain is, how far the patient can walk before it starts, whether that distance has changed, and how long rest takes to relieve it.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 18

src.question: Which history question best measures claudication?
src.key: How far can you walk before pain?
src.explanation: The history asks where the pain is, how far the patient can walk before it starts, whether that distance has changed, and how long rest takes to relieve it.

items.section_title: 1.3 · Arterial thrombosis and embolism: acute limb ischemia and atheroembolism audio after 10/01
items.html: Immediately threatened limb. A limb that is immediately threatened is salvageable only with immediate revascularization, so it should preferentially undergo further evaluation and treatment in a surgical suite, without delay.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 63

src.question: A 74-year-old man with sudden leg ischemia has sensory loss extending beyond the toes with rest pain, mild-to-moderate weakness, an inaudible arterial Doppler signal and an audible venous signal. Where should his evaluation and treatment take place?
src.key: In the surgical suite, without delay
src.explanation: An immediately threatened limb is salvageable only with immediate revascularization, so it should preferentially undergo further evaluation and treatment in a surgical suite.

items.section_title: 1.2 · Peripheral artery disease (and critical limb ischemia) audio after 10/01
items.html: Smoking and peripheral artery disease. Cigarette smoking triples the risk of peripheral artery disease compared with nonsmokers, and smoking cessation heads the list of risk-factor reduction measures for every patient with the disease.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 50

src.question: A 58-year-old man who smokes a pack a day has calf claudication and an ankle-brachial index of 0.7. He asks what matters most for his legs. Which counseling point is most important?
src.explanation: Cigarette smoking triples the risk of peripheral artery disease compared with nonsmokers, and smoking cessation heads the list of risk-factor reduction measures for every patient with the disease.

items.section_title: 1.2 · Peripheral artery disease (and critical limb ischemia) audio after 10/01
items.html: Antiplatelet therapy in peripheral artery disease. Aspirin or clopidogrel lower the risk of myocardial infarction and stroke; cilostazol (also a vasodilator) is added to improve walking distance.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 51

src.question: A 66-year-old man with claudication and an ankle-brachial index of 0.72 has no bleeding history. Which medication class should be started to lower his risk of myocardial infarction and stroke?
src.explanation: Antiplatelet therapy (aspirin, clopidogrel or cilostazol) decreases the overall risk of cardiovascular disease from myocardial infarction and stroke and improves walking distance in peripheral artery disease.

items.html: Laboratory results in Takotsubo (stress) cardiomyopathy. Troponin I and T are usually elevated and B-type natriuretic peptide is frequently elevated, which adds to the resemblance to acute coronary syndrome.

src.question: Which laboratory results are typical of Takotsubo (stress) cardiomyopathy?
src.explanation: Troponin I and T are usually elevated and B-type natriuretic peptide is frequently elevated, which adds to the resemblance to acute coronary syndrome.

items.html: SKIP

src.question: In dilated cardiomyopathy, which patients receive anticoagulation?
src.key: Atrial fibrillation, prosthetic valve or clot
src.explanation: Anticoagulants should be restricted to patients in atrial fibrillation, with artificial valves or with a known mural thrombus.

items.note: Removed 2026-10-15: anticoagulation indications in dilated cardiomyopathy are only in slide 42's speaker notes (Jaxon: notes are not slide content).

items.html: Myocarditis work-up. Serum troponin is the indicator of cardiac myonecrosis. The rest of the work-up adds leukocytosis on the blood count, a possibly elevated sedimentation rate and electrocardiogram changes.

src.question: A 24-year-old woman with chest pain and breathlessness after a recent viral illness is being evaluated for myocarditis. Her electrocardiogram shows sinus tachycardia. Which laboratory result would indicate cardiac myonecrosis?
src.explanation: Serum troponin is the indicator of cardiac myonecrosis in myocarditis. The rest of the work-up adds leukocytosis on the blood count, a possibly elevated sedimentation rate and electrocardiogram changes.

items.html: Prognosis of symptomatic dilated cardiomyopathy. Once symptoms emerge, prognosis is poor overall, with 50% mortality at five years, largely from progressive disease and sudden cardiac death due to arrhythmia. The course depends on response to therapy.

src.question: A 60-year-old man has just been diagnosed with symptomatic idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy and an ejection fraction of 25%. He asks what his long-term outlook is. Which statement about his prognosis is most accurate?
src.key: About half die within five years
src.explanation: Once symptoms emerge, prognosis is poor overall, with 50% mortality at five years, largely from progressive disease and sudden cardiac death due to arrhythmia. The course depends on response to therapy.

items.html: Cardiac rehabilitation. Cardiac rehabilitation programs improve exercise tolerance and quality of life, with education on medication adherence, nutrition and symptom monitoring, and psychological support for chronic illness.

src.question: A 66-year-old man with stable cardiomyopathy on full medical therapy says he tires after walking a block and feels anxious about exercising. He has no symptoms at rest. Which referral is most appropriate to improve his exercise tolerance?
src.explanation: Cardiac rehabilitation programs improve exercise tolerance and quality of life, with education on medication adherence, nutrition and symptom monitoring, and psychological support for chronic illness.

items.html: Adolescents and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Age-specific strategies include genetic screening, and disease detected in a family member is a common reason evaluation begins. The condition is autosomal dominant, so one affected parent is enough to pass it on.

src.question: A 15-year-old boy is seen for a sports physical. He has no symptoms, but his father was recently diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, which is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern. Which strategy for this adolescent is most appropriate?
src.explanation: Age-specific strategies for adolescents include genetic screening for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and disease detected in a family member is a common reason evaluation begins. One affected parent is enough to pass it on.

items.html: Nitrates in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Drugs that reduce preload or afterload, such as nitrates, may increase symptoms by aggravating outflow tract obstruction, so nitroglycerin should be avoided if possible.

src.question: A 41-year-old man with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy comes to the emergency department with exertional chest pressure. His electrocardiogram shows left ventricular hypertrophy without acute changes, and a clinician reaches for a chest pain order set. Which medication should be avoided?
src.explanation: Drugs that reduce preload or afterload, such as nitrates, may increase symptoms by aggravating outflow tract obstruction, so nitroglycerin should be avoided if possible in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

items.html: Palliative care in cardiomyopathy. It covers symptom management of dyspnea, fatigue and edema, advance care planning and goals-of-care discussions, support for caregivers, and hospice referral in end-stage disease.

src.question: An 86-year-old woman with end-stage cardiomyopathy has breathlessness at rest, edema and fatigue despite maximal tolerated therapy. She is not a transplant or device candidate and says she wants comfort at home. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Discuss goals of care and hospice
src.explanation: Palliative care in cardiomyopathy covers symptom management of dyspnea, fatigue and edema, advance care planning and goals-of-care discussions, support for caregivers, and hospice referral in end-stage disease.

items.html: Cardiac catheterization in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. It is not required for the diagnosis; it is obtained only when invasive therapy such as a pacemaker or surgery is planned.

src.question: A 33-year-old man with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy confirmed by echocardiography has typical findings and no plans for surgery or a device. A colleague suggests cardiac catheterization to complete the work-up. When is cardiac catheterization indicated in this condition?
src.key: Only if surgery or a pacemaker is planned
src.explanation: Cardiac catheterization is not required for the diagnosis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; it is obtained when invasive therapy such as a pacemaker or surgery is planned.

items.html: Activity restriction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Activity restriction for high-risk individuals is an adolescent strategy, because sudden death is highest in preadolescents and adolescents and is related to extreme exertion.

src.question: A 16-year-old girl with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy has had an episode of fainting during basketball practice and brief runs of ventricular tachycardia on monitoring. She wants to keep playing on her competitive school team. Which counseling point is most appropriate?
src.key: Activity restriction given her high risk
src.explanation: Activity restriction for high-risk individuals is an adolescent strategy, and sudden death in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is highest in preadolescents and adolescents and is related to extreme exertion.

items.section_title: 1.2 · Peripheral artery disease (and critical limb ischemia) audio after 10/01
items.html: Acute limb ischemia. Numbness over the dorsum of the foot is often the earliest neurologic sign, because light-touch sensory fibers are highly susceptible to ischemia.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 61

src.question: What is often the earliest neurologic sign of acute limb ischemia?
src.key: Numbness over the dorsum of the foot
src.explanation: Light-touch sensory fibers are highly susceptible to ischemia, so sensory deficits over the dorsum of the foot are often the earliest neurologic sign of acute vascular insufficiency.

items.html: Amaurosis fugax. Interrupted blood flow to the retina causes transient loss of vision in one eye, a rapid fading like a curtain descending, and is a focal symptom of carotid disease.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 72

src.question: What is amaurosis fugax?
src.key: Transient loss of vision in one eye
src.explanation: Amaurosis fugax is interrupted blood flow to the retina causing transient monocular blindness, a rapid fading of vision like a curtain descending, a focal symptom of carotid disease.

items.section_title: 1.2 · Peripheral artery disease (and critical limb ischemia) audio after 10/01
items.html: Ischemic rest pain. It responds poorly to analgesics, even narcotics, and is relieved instead by dependency, hanging the leg over the bed or walking around.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 21

src.question: How does ischemic rest pain respond to analgesics?
src.explanation: Ischemic rest pain is not readily controlled by analgesics, even narcotics; it is relieved instead by dependency, hanging the leg over the bed or walking around.

items.section_title: 1.5 · Aortic aneurysms: abdominal, thoracic and false audio after 10/01
items.html: Thoracic aortic aneurysms. Most are asymptomatic and found incidentally on chest radiograph; a history of hypertension is common, and symptoms depend on location.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 104

src.question: How are most thoracic aortic aneurysms found?
src.explanation: Most thoracic aortic aneurysms are asymptomatic and found incidentally on chest radiograph; a history of hypertension is common, and symptoms depend on location.

items.section_title: 1.2 · Peripheral artery disease (and critical limb ischemia) audio after 10/01
items.html: Ischemic ulcers of critical limb ischemia. They usually appear at the toe tips and between digits, where arterial branches terminate, and at areas of increased focal pressure such as the metatarsal heads.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 37

src.question: Where do ischemic ulcers of critical limb ischemia usually appear?
src.explanation: Ulcers form where arterial branches terminate, at the tips of the toes and between digits, and at areas of increased focal pressure such as the metatarsal heads.

items.html: Ejection fraction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. It is usually normal, and in late stages it rises above 75% because the small ventricle nearly empties to maintain output.

src.question: What happens to ejection fraction in late-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy?
src.explanation: The ejection fraction is usually normal, and in late stages it is elevated above 75% because the small ventricle nearly empties to maintain output.

items.html: Cardiac rehabilitation in cardiomyopathy. Programs aim for better exercise tolerance and quality of life, with education on medications, nutrition and symptom monitoring and psychological support.

src.question: What is the aim of cardiac rehabilitation programs in cardiomyopathy?
src.key: Better exercise tolerance and quality of life
src.explanation: Cardiac rehabilitation programs aim to improve exercise tolerance and quality of life, with education on medications, nutrition and symptom monitoring and psychological support.

items.html: Pacemaker in restrictive cardiomyopathy. Nodal fibrosis of the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes can cause heart block, so a permanent pacemaker is placed for conduction system disease.

src.question: Why may a permanent pacemaker be needed in restrictive cardiomyopathy?
src.explanation: Fibrosis of the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes can lead to heart block, so a permanent pacemaker is placed for conduction system disease.

items.html: Diuretics in restrictive cardiomyopathy. They treat pulmonary and systemic congestion but are used with caution, because they lower preload and stiff ventricles need preload to maintain cardiac output.

src.question: Why must diuretics be used cautiously in restrictive cardiomyopathy?
src.explanation: Diuretics treat pulmonary and systemic congestion, but they lower preload, and noncompliant ventricles depend on preload to maintain cardiac output.

also.key: Use with caution; stiff ventricles need preload
also.explanation: Diuretics are used for pulmonary and systemic congestion in restrictive cardiomyopathy, but with caution, because they lower preload and the noncompliant ventricles depend on preload to maintain cardiac output.

items.html: Restrictive cardiomyopathy on echocardiogram. Marked enlargement of one or both atria (big atria) with near-normal ventricles: near-normal left ventricular systolic function and cavity size, preserved ejection fraction and abnormal diastolic function.

src.question: Which echocardiogram pattern fits restrictive cardiomyopathy?
src.explanation: The echocardiogram shows marked enlargement of one or both atria, near-normal left ventricular systolic function and cavity size, preserved ejection fraction and abnormal diastolic function.

items.html: Gastrointestinal findings of dilated cardiomyopathy. Congestive enlargement of the liver (hepatomegaly), hepatojugular reflux and ascites, all from venous congestion as the failing heart backs up blood.

src.question: A 64-year-old woman with dilated cardiomyopathy has breathlessness on exertion and peripheral edema. On examination her neck veins distend when firm pressure is held over her right upper abdomen, a sign called hepatojugular reflux (neck-vein distension with firm pressure over the liver). Which additional finding is expected with this degree of congestion?
src.explanation: The gastrointestinal findings of dilated cardiomyopathy are congestive hepatomegaly, hepatojugular reflux and ascites, all from venous congestion as the failing heart backs up blood.

items.html: Mitral regurgitation in dilated cardiomyopathy. As the ventricle dilates, the valve apparatus is distorted, so functional mitral regurgitation, appearing earlier, and tricuspid regurgitation commonly develop; the mitral murmur is holosystolic at the apex, radiating to the axilla.

src.question: A 66-year-old woman with dilated cardiomyopathy develops a new holosystolic murmur heard best at the apex that radiates to the left axilla. Her ventricle has continued to enlarge on serial echocardiograms. Which complication best accounts for the new murmur?
src.explanation: As the ventricle dilates, the valve apparatus is distorted, and mitral regurgitation (which appears earlier) and tricuspid regurgitation commonly develop. The mitral murmur is holosystolic at the apex, radiating to the axilla.

items.html: SKIP

src.question: A 59-year-old man with dilated cardiomyopathy, sinus rhythm and an ejection fraction of 20% has a follow-up echocardiogram that shows a thrombus layered against the wall of the left ventricle. Which additional treatment is now indicated?
src.explanation: Dilated ventricles carry a risk of thromboembolic complications, and a known mural thrombus is one of the three indications for anticoagulation in dilated cardiomyopathy, with atrial fibrillation and an artificial valve.

items.note: Removed 2026-10-15: anticoagulation indications in dilated cardiomyopathy are only in slide 42's speaker notes (Jaxon: notes are not slide content).

items.section_title: 1.3 · Arterial thrombosis and embolism: acute limb ischemia and atheroembolism audio after 10/01
items.html: Acute limb ischemia and imaging. Viable and marginally threatened limbs have sufficient time for vascular imaging such as computed tomography angiography; immediately threatened limbs go to a surgical suite.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 62

src.question: Which acute limb ischemia categories leave time for vascular imaging?
src.explanation: Viable and marginally threatened limbs have sufficient time for vascular imaging such as computed tomography angiography; immediately threatened limbs go to a surgical suite.

items.html: Takotsubo (stress) cardiomyopathy treatment. Supportive treatment depends on presentation: anticoagulation if a left ventricular thrombus is present, diuretics if heart failure is present, and beta blockers.

src.question: When is anticoagulation given in Takotsubo (stress) cardiomyopathy?
src.key: If a ventricular thrombus is present
src.explanation: Supportive treatment depends on presentation: anticoagulation if a left ventricular thrombus is present, diuretics if heart failure is present, and beta blockers.

items.html: Restrictive cardiomyopathy testing. Cardiac catheterization is useful to evaluate ventricular pressure tracings, alongside cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and, when needed, endomyocardial biopsy.

src.question: A 67-year-old woman with suspected restrictive cardiomyopathy has right-sided heart failure and big atria on echocardiogram. Her cardiologist wants to measure pressures inside both ventricles to characterize the filling problem. Which invasive test evaluates ventricular pressure tracings?
src.explanation: Cardiac catheterization is useful in restrictive cardiomyopathy to evaluate ventricular pressure tracings, alongside cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and, when needed, endomyocardial biopsy.

items.html: Carotid stenosis. Asymptomatic patients with significant carotid stenosis outnumber symptomatic patients by 4:1, which is why carotid disease is often found before any stroke or attack.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 72

src.question: By what ratio do asymptomatic patients with significant carotid stenosis outnumber symptomatic ones?
src.explanation: Asymptomatic patients with significant carotid stenosis outnumber symptomatic patients by 4:1, which is why carotid disease is often found before any stroke or attack.

items.section_title: 1.2 · Peripheral artery disease (and critical limb ischemia) audio after 10/01
items.html: Ankle-brachial index. A value between 0.4 and 0.9 is the claudication band, matching exertional calf pain relieved by rest; the lower of the two legs is taken as the overall index.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 42

src.question: A 70-year-old man with hypertension reports calf pain after walking about two blocks that resolves with rest. His ankle-brachial index is 0.62 on the left and normal on the right. Which interpretation fits the left-sided value?
src.explanation: An ankle-brachial index between 0.4 and 0.9 is the claudication band, matching exertional calf pain relieved by rest. The lower of the two legs is taken as the overall index.

items.html: Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy refractory to drugs. Surgical septal myectomy excises part of the septal myocardium causing outflow obstruction, and mitral regurgitation from systolic anterior motion may resolve with myectomy alone, without valve replacement.

src.question: A 38-year-old woman with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy still has disabling breathlessness despite a beta blocker and later verapamil. Echocardiogram shows systolic anterior motion (the anterior mitral leaflet pulled into the outflow tract) with mitral regurgitation. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.explanation: Surgical myectomy excises part of the septal myocardium causing outflow obstruction, and the mitral regurgitation from systolic anterior motion may resolve with myectomy alone, without valve replacement.

items.html: B-type natriuretic peptide. It is released when ventricular filling pressures are high; a level below 100 pg/mL makes heart failure an unlikely explanation for the current symptoms.

src.question: A 63-year-old woman with dilated cardiomyopathy comes to clinic with mild breathlessness on exertion. Her examination shows trace ankle edema and clear lungs. Her B-type natriuretic peptide is 60 pg/mL. What does this natriuretic peptide result indicate?
src.explanation: B-type natriuretic peptide is released when ventricular filling pressures are high, and a level below 100 pg/mL excludes heart failure as the explanation for her current symptoms.

items.html: Sudden death risk in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Ambulatory electrocardiogram monitoring for 24 to 48 hours should be performed to assess the risk of ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death.

src.question: A 25-year-old woman has newly diagnosed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with a septum of 2.2 cm and occasional palpitations. Her cardiologist wants to judge her risk of ventricular arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death. Which test assesses that risk?
src.explanation: Ambulatory electrocardiogram monitoring for 24 to 48 hours should be performed in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy to assess the risk of ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death.

items.html: Thrombolysis. Thrombolysis, in which tissue plasminogen activator breaks down the clot, is considered for a large proximal deep vein thrombosis or a stable pulmonary embolism.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slide 70

src.question: For which clot may thrombolysis be considered in deep vein thrombosis?
src.explanation: Correct. Thrombolysis, in which tissue plasminogen activator breaks down the clot, is considered for a large proximal deep vein thrombosis or a stable pulmonary embolism.

items.html: Prior deep vein thrombosis and chronic venous insufficiency. Prior deep vein thrombosis, through valve scarring and obstruction, is one of the most common causes of chronic venous insufficiency; when that happens the condition is called post-thrombotic syndrome.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slide 11

src.question: Prior deep vein thrombosis is one of the most common causes of which chronic condition?
src.explanation: Correct. Prior deep vein thrombosis, through valve scarring and obstruction, is one of the most common causes of chronic venous insufficiency, also called post-thrombotic syndrome.

items.html: Wells score items and the moderate band. A previously documented deep vein thrombosis adds 1 point, swelling of the entire leg adds 1 point, and recent plaster immobilization adds 1 point. A total of 1 to 2 is the moderate band.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slide 55

src.question: A 47-year-old woman with a previous deep vein thrombosis two years ago comes to the emergency department with swelling of the entire right leg. She has no pitting edema, calf asymmetry over 3 cm, tenderness along the deep veins, collateral veins, cancer, recent bed rest, surgery or cast, and no better alternative diagnosis. By the Wells criteria, which likelihood category applies?
src.explanation: Correct. A previously documented deep vein thrombosis adds 1 point and swelling of the entire leg adds 1 point, for 2 in total, the moderate band of 1 to 2. Moderate likelihood leads to a D-dimer next. Correct. Recent plaster immobilization and pitting edema in the symptomatic leg give a Wells score of 2, a moderate pretest probability. Patients scoring 1 to 2 need a D-dimer, and a negative result rules out the diagnosis.

also.explanation: Correct. Recent plaster immobilization and pitting edema in the symptomatic leg give a Wells score of 2, a moderate pretest probability. Patients scoring 1 to 2 need a D-dimer, and a negative result rules out the diagnosis. A 44-year-old man seen in an outpatient clinic has had left calf pain and swelling for three days. A plaster cast was removed from his left leg yesterday after four weeks for a tibial fracture. Examination shows pitting edema confined to the left leg. He meets no other Wells criteria, and no alternative diagnosis is judged as likely as deep vein thrombosis. Which is the most appropriate next test?

items.html: Outpatient treatment of deep vein thrombosis. Outpatient therapy suits patients who are hemodynamically stable, have low bleeding risk and no renal insufficiency, and have good support with reliable follow-up. It is not appropriate for iliofemoral proximal clots, concurrent symptomatic pulmonary embolism, high bleeding risk or comorbidities needing inpatient care.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slide 65

src.question: A 48-year-old man with a first calf deep vein thrombosis is hemodynamically stable, has low bleeding risk and normal kidney function, and has a supportive spouse who will bring him to every follow-up visit. Which is the best setting for treatment?
src.explanation: Correct. Outpatient therapy suits patients who are hemodynamically stable, have low bleeding risk and no renal insufficiency, and have good support with reliable follow-up. He meets every criterion. Correct. Outpatient therapy is not appropriate for iliofemoral proximal clots, concurrent symptomatic pulmonary embolism, high bleeding risk or comorbidities needing inpatient care.

also.explanation: Correct. Outpatient therapy is not appropriate for iliofemoral proximal clots, concurrent symptomatic pulmonary embolism, high bleeding risk or comorbidities needing inpatient care. Which finding makes outpatient therapy for deep vein thrombosis inappropriate?

items.html: Duplex ultrasound in chronic venous insufficiency. Duplex ultrasound assesses venous patency and valve competence, and chronic venous insufficiency shows incompetent valves with reflux, which fail to stop blood flowing back toward the foot.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slide 28

src.question: A 61-year-old woman with prior deep vein thrombosis has leg edema and brown pigmentation. Duplex ultrasound is performed to explain her symptoms. Which finding is expected?
src.explanation: Correct. Duplex ultrasound assesses venous patency and valve competence, and chronic venous insufficiency shows valves that fail to stop blood flowing back toward the foot, producing venous hypertension.

items.html: Constrictive pericarditis on imaging. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging helps separate restrictive cardiomyopathy from constrictive pericarditis, and a thickened pericardium points to constrictive pericarditis rather than restrictive cardiomyopathy, though constriction can occur with a normal-thickness pericardium.

src.question: A 69-year-old woman with right-sided heart failure, ascites and a raised jugular venous pressure has cardiac magnetic resonance imaging to decide between restrictive cardiomyopathy and constrictive pericarditis. Which imaging finding would point to constrictive pericarditis instead?
src.explanation: Correct. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging helps separate the two conditions, and a thickened pericardium points to constrictive pericarditis rather than restrictive cardiomyopathy, though constriction can occur with a normal-thickness pericardium.

items.html: High likelihood, negative thigh ultrasound. In the high-likelihood pathway a negative thigh ultrasound is followed by lower-leg ultrasound, phlebography or a repeat thigh ultrasound in 1 week; active cancer, entire leg swelling, calf swelling over 3 cm and pitting edema give a high Wells score of 4.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slides 55-56, 61 (Wells table and flowchart pictures)

src.question: A 61-year-old man receiving chemotherapy for lung cancer has had swelling of his whole left leg for four days, with pitting edema in that leg and a calf 4 cm larger than the right. An ultrasound of the thigh veins shows no clot. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Repeat the thigh scan in a week
src.explanation: Correct. Active cancer, entire leg swelling, calf swelling over 3 cm and pitting edema give a high Wells score of 4. In the high-likelihood pathway a negative thigh ultrasound is followed by lower-leg ultrasound, phlebography or a repeat thigh ultrasound in 1 week.

items.html: Low likelihood, negative thigh ultrasound. In the low likelihood pathway a positive D-dimer leads to ultrasound of the thigh, and a negative ultrasound ends the work-up; the repeat and extra imaging options belong to the high likelihood pathway.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slides 56, 57 (flowchart picture)

src.question: In the low likelihood Wells category, a patient's D-dimer is positive and the thigh ultrasound that follows shows no clot. What is the next step?
src.explanation: Correct. In the low likelihood pathway a positive D-dimer leads to ultrasound of the thigh, and a negative ultrasound ends the work-up; the repeat and extra imaging options belong to the high likelihood pathway.

items.html: High likelihood, negative D-dimer. With a high Wells score the D-dimer is skipped, or if it was drawn, a negative result does not end the evaluation: the patient still goes to venous duplex ultrasound.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slide 56 (flowchart picture)

src.question: A 62-year-old woman on chemotherapy for breast cancer comes to the emergency department with a calf 4 cm larger than the other, tenderness along the deep veins and no better explanation, so her Wells score is high. Her D-dimer, drawn at triage, is negative. Which action should be avoided?
src.key: Ending the work-up at the D-dimer
src.explanation: Correct. With a high Wells score the D-dimer is skipped, or if it was drawn, a negative result does not end the evaluation: she still goes to venous duplex ultrasound. Stopping here risks missing a clot with high pretest probability.

items.html: Digoxin in dilated cardiomyopathy. Digoxin is on the list of drugs used to manage dilated cardiomyopathy, but it is considered a second-line drug, added after core therapy such as a beta blocker and an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor.

src.question: A 64-year-old man with dilated cardiomyopathy takes a beta blocker, an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor and a diuretic. His clinician mentions that digoxin may be added later. Which statement describes the place of digoxin in his treatment?
src.explanation: Correct. Digoxin is on the list of drugs used to manage dilated cardiomyopathy, but it is considered a second-line drug, added after core therapy such as a beta blocker and an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor.

items.html: Fungal endocarditis. In fungal endocarditis the most likely complication is embolism and occlusion of larger peripheral arteries from embolization.

src.question: What is the most likely complication of fungal infective endocarditis?
src.explanation: Correct. In fungal endocarditis the most likely complication is embolism and occlusion of larger peripheral arteries from embolization.

items.html: Chagas disease and complete block. Chagas disease, a parasitic infection, is a named cause of complete heart block, listed among the causes of complete block with Lyme carditis, bacterial endocarditis with an abscess and inflammatory or infiltrative disease.

src.question: Which parasitic infection is a named cause of third-degree (complete) atrioventricular block?
src.explanation: Correct. Chagas disease is listed among the causes of complete block, with Lyme carditis, bacterial endocarditis with an abscess and inflammatory or infiltrative disease.

also.explanation: Correct. Chagas disease is a named cause of complete heart block; it is a parasitic infection endemic in parts of Latin America such as rural Bolivia. A 45-year-old man who grew up in rural Bolivia has months of fatigue and exertional breathlessness. His heart rate is 38 and the electrocardiogram shows P waves completely dissociated from slow, wide QRS complexes. Which infection is a named cause of his conduction disease?

items.html: Older adults with an effusion. In older adults there is a higher index of suspicion for malignancy, especially with an effusion or tamponade.

src.question: An 81-year-old man with 3 months of weight loss presents with dyspnea and a large pericardial effusion. He has had no recent viral illness, chest surgery or radiation. Which etiology should be most strongly suspected?
src.explanation: Correct. In older adults there is a higher index of suspicion for malignancy, especially with an effusion or tamponade, and his weight loss without a viral prodrome reinforces it.

items.section_title: 6.4 · Acute pericarditis: risk, treatment, prognosis and counseling
items.html: Oral anticoagulants in acute pericarditis. Patients on oral anticoagulants are among the higher-risk groups for acute pericarditis (with fever, subacute course, tamponade signs, large effusion, immunosuppression, trauma and raised troponin) and potentially need hospitalization.

src.question: A 45-year-old woman taking warfarin for a mechanical valve presents with 2 days of sharp chest pain eased by leaning forward, widespread ST elevation and a small effusion. She is afebrile and her blood pressure is 128/78. Which is the most appropriate disposition?
src.explanation: Correct. Patients on oral anticoagulants are among the higher-risk groups for acute pericarditis (with fever, subacute course, tamponade signs, large effusion, immunosuppression, trauma, raised troponin) and potentially need hospitalization.

items.html: Health care-associated endocarditis. Health care-associated endocarditis should be suspected in hospitalized patients who develop fevers and positive blood cultures without an apparent source; Staphylococcus aureus causes about half of these cases.

src.question: A 63-year-old woman has been in the hospital for 9 days after hip surgery. She develops a new fever, and two sets of blood cultures grow Staphylococcus aureus; she has no indwelling catheter, and examination finds no wound or other source. Which diagnosis must be suspected?
src.explanation: Correct. Health care-associated endocarditis should be suspected in hospitalized patients who develop fevers and positive blood cultures without an apparent source; Staphylococcus aureus causes about half of these cases.

items.html: Indications for surgery. Heart failure from valve dysfunction, infection not resolving on appropriate antibiotic therapy, abscess and fungal infection are indications for surgery. Fungal infection is difficult to cure with medications alone, so the referral is to cardiothoracic surgery.

src.question: A 56-year-old man on chemotherapy has Candida endocarditis confirmed on blood cultures and echocardiography. Which referral is most appropriate in addition to infectious disease?
src.explanation: Correct. Fungal infection is difficult to cure with medications alone and is an indication for surgery, so cardiothoracic surgery evaluates him.

also.explanation: Correct. Abscess is an indication for surgery, alongside heart failure from valve dysfunction, infection not resolving on appropriate antibiotics and fungal infection, so cardiothoracic surgery evaluates her. A 66-year-old woman with aortic valve endocarditis has a transesophageal echocardiogram that shows an abscess around the valve ring. Which is the most appropriate next step?

Correct. Infection not resolving with appropriate antibiotic therapy is an indication for surgery, as are heart failure from valve dysfunction, abscess and fungal infection. A 53-year-old man has had positive blood cultures for 10 days despite an antibiotic regimen that matches his organism's sensitivities, and he still has fevers. Which is the most appropriate next step?

items.html: What mimics acute tamponade. The differential of acute tamponade includes myocardial infarction (especially with right ventricular involvement), aortic dissection and massive pulmonary embolism, which can all mimic it.

src.question: A 71-year-old man with a new inferior myocardial infarction involving the right ventricle is hypotensive with distended jugular veins and clear lungs. Tamponade is considered. Why must his infarction stay on the differential?
src.explanation: Correct. The differential of acute tamponade includes myocardial infarction (especially with right ventricular involvement), aortic dissection and massive pulmonary embolism, which can all mimic it.

items.html: Organisms of acute endocarditis. An abrupt, toxic, high-fever course is acute endocarditis, caused by virulent organisms such as Staphylococcus aureus and beta-hemolytic streptococci.

src.question: A 55-year-old man has 3 days of fever to 40.0 °C (104.0 °F), rigors and a new murmur, and he looks toxic. Which organism is a classic cause of this tempo of infective endocarditis?
src.explanation: Correct. An abrupt, toxic, high-fever course is acute endocarditis, caused by virulent organisms such as Staphylococcus aureus and beta-hemolytic streptococci.

items.html: Inflammatory markers in acute pericarditis. The initial workup includes complete blood count, troponins, erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein; the C-reactive protein is checked at presentation and weekly to guide tapering.

src.question: A 29-year-old woman has acute pericarditis with a friction rub (a scratchy, squeaking sound) and widespread ST elevation. Her clinician wants laboratory values that confirm inflammation and can guide the length of therapy. Which pair of tests is most appropriate?
src.explanation: Correct. The initial workup includes complete blood count, troponins, erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein; the C-reactive protein is checked at presentation and weekly to guide tapering.

items.html: Device leads and the Virchow triad. Damage to the vessel lining from an indwelling device is endothelial trauma, one leg of the Virchow triad. Pacemakers, implanted defibrillators and central venous catheters are the most common causes of upper-extremity deep vein thrombosis.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slide 47

src.question: A 52-year-old man with a pacemaker implanted two weeks ago has three days of swelling and aching of the left arm. The pacemaker lead has injured the wall of the subclavian vein. Which component of the Virchow triad does this injury represent?
src.explanation: Correct. Damage to the vessel lining from an indwelling device is endothelial trauma, one leg of the Virchow triad. Pacemakers, implanted defibrillators and central venous catheters are the most common causes of upper-extremity deep vein thrombosis.

items.html: Upper extremity deep vein thrombosis. Upper extremity deep vein thrombosis often presents only with limb swelling and arm discomfort, and indwelling central venous catheters are a leading cause. Duplex ultrasound of the involved limb is the test.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slide 51

src.question: A 26-year-old woman had a peripherally inserted central catheter placed in her right arm two weeks ago for long-term antibiotic therapy. She reports aching and swelling of the arm. Examination shows diffuse swelling of the entire right upper arm with mild redness, and there is no palpable cord and no purulent drainage. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: Venous duplex ultrasound of the arm
src.explanation: Correct. Upper extremity deep vein thrombosis often presents only with limb swelling and arm discomfort, and indwelling central venous catheters are a leading cause. Duplex ultrasound of the involved limb is the test.

items.html: Nonhealing venous ulcers. Nonhealing ulcers are referred to a vascular specialist, and an ulcer that has not healed in four to six months needs further workup for infection or other causes.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slide 37

src.question: A 70-year-old woman with a medial ankle venous ulcer has used compression, elevation and wound care for seven months and the ulcer has not healed. Which referral is most appropriate?
src.explanation: Correct. Nonhealing ulcers are on the list for referral to a vascular specialist; healing can take 4 to 6 months, and an ulcer still open after that needs further workup for infection or other causes.

items.html: Superficial thrombophlebitis. Tenderness, induration and erythema along a superficial vein, with an indurated palpable cord after recent catheter use, is superficial thrombophlebitis. Redness confined to the vein argues against infection.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slide 76

src.question: A 34-year-old woman has been hospitalized for four days receiving intravenous antibiotics through a peripheral catheter in her left forearm. She now has pain, redness and warmth along the course of the vein, and a firm, tender, palpable cord can be felt beneath the skin. She is afebrile, and the redness stays within the line of the vein. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
src.explanation: Correct. Tenderness, induration and erythema along a superficial vein, with an indurated palpable cord after recent catheter use, is superficial thrombophlebitis. Redness confined to the vein argues against infection.

items.section_title: 2.3 · Arterial thrombosis and embolism: acute limb ischemia and atheroembolism audio after 10/01
items.html: Warning signs after an embolic occlusion. The six P's of arterial assessment (pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis and poikilothermia) mark acute limb ischemia, a vascular emergency that needs immediate care.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 61

src.question: A 67-year-old man with atrial fibrillation is being discharged after treatment of an embolic leg occlusion. Which warning symptoms should prompt him to return immediately?
src.explanation: Correct. The six P's of arterial assessment (pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis and poikilothermia) mark acute limb ischemia, a vascular emergency that needs immediate care.

items.html: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the family. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is mostly inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, so one affected parent is enough to pass it on, and detection in a family member is a common reason evaluation of first-degree relatives begins.

src.question: A 20-year-old man has just been diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy on echocardiography. He has two younger sisters and a brother. His mother had unexplained sudden death at 44. Which step for his family is most appropriate?
src.explanation: Correct. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is mostly inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, so one affected parent is enough to pass it on, and detection in a family member is a common reason evaluation of relatives begins.

items.html: Medications that cause pericardial effusion. Medication causes of pericardial effusion include doxorubicin, minoxidil, phenytoin, and hydralazine and procainamide through drug-induced lupus.

src.question: Which medication is a recognized cause of pericardial effusion?
src.explanation: Correct. Medication causes of pericardial effusion include doxorubicin, minoxidil, phenytoin, and hydralazine and procainamide through drug-induced lupus.

items.html: Reversing dabigatran. Idarucizumab reverses dabigatran in life-threatening or intracranial hemorrhage; each reversal agent is specific to its anticoagulant.
cites: CMS I - Venous Disorders - Shah Fallsv UPDATED.pptx, Slide 68

src.question: Idarucizumab is the reversal agent for which anticoagulant?
src.explanation: Correct. Idarucizumab reverses dabigatran in life-threatening or intracranial hemorrhage; each reversal agent is specific to its anticoagulant.

items.html: Maneuvers that soften the obstructive murmur. Anything that increases blood flow in the heart reduces outflow obstruction and softens the murmur. Handgrip raises afterload, and squatting or passive leg raising raise preload, so all three decrease the murmur.

src.question: A 27-year-old woman with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is examined by a student who hears a loud systolic murmur at the left sternal border. Respiration does not change it. Which bedside maneuver would soften her murmur?
src.explanation: Correct. Anything that increases blood flow in the heart reduces outflow obstruction and softens the murmur. Handgrip raises afterload, and squatting or passive leg raising raise preload, so all three decrease the murmur.

items.html: Recognizing monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. A regular wide QRS rhythm of 100 to 250 per minute with identical complexes lasting over 30 seconds is sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia, often seen after myocardial infarction.

src.question: A 66-year-old man with a large anterior myocardial infarction two years ago has palpitations and lightheadedness. He is alert, with a blood pressure of 112/70. The monitor shows a regular wide QRS rhythm at 170 per minute with no P waves, every complex the same shape, for over a minute. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
src.explanation: Correct. A regular wide QRS rhythm of 100 to 250 per minute without P waves, with identical complexes lasting over 30 seconds, is sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia, often seen after myocardial infarction.

items.html: Transesophageal echocardiography and the Duke criteria. Transesophageal echocardiography is required for optimal assessment of possible prosthetic valve endocarditis or complicated endocarditis; it is highly sensitive and specific.

src.question: Under the modified Duke criteria, in which situation is transesophageal echocardiography required for optimal assessment?
src.explanation: Correct. Transesophageal echocardiography is required for optimal assessment of possible prosthetic valve endocarditis or complicated endocarditis; it is highly sensitive and specific.

items.section_title: 5.10 · Sudden cardiac death and the implantable defibrillator
items.html: Risk without an infarction. Coronary artery disease is the most common predisposing condition for sudden cardiac death, even in adults without a history of myocardial infarction, so the risk exists before any heart attack.

src.question: A 59-year-old man with stable coronary artery disease, who has never had a heart attack, asks whether he is at any risk of sudden cardiac death. Which statement is accurate?
src.key: Risk exists even without an infarction
src.explanation: Correct. Coronary artery disease is the most common predisposing condition for sudden cardiac death, even in adults without a history of myocardial infarction, so his risk does not wait for a heart attack.

items.html: Care of the underlying condition. Right bundle branch block is usually asymptomatic, and its treatment depends on the underlying condition; prognosis depends on the presence and type of heart disease.

src.question: A 66-year-old man has a right bundle branch block found on routine testing. He has no symptoms, and his examination is normal. Which approach to treatment is correct?
src.explanation: Correct. Right bundle branch block is usually asymptomatic, and its treatment depends on the underlying condition; prognosis depends on the presence and type of heart disease.

items.html: Transient ischemic attack. A transient ischemic attack is a focal deficit, a focal loss of neurologic function lasting less than 24 hours; it and stroke classify a patient with carotid disease as symptomatic.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 72

src.question: What defines a transient ischemic attack?
src.explanation: Correct. A transient ischemic attack is a focal loss of neurologic function lasting less than 24 hours; it and stroke classify a patient with carotid disease as symptomatic.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Peripheral artery disease (and critical limb ischemia) audio after 10/01
items.html: Rest pain on the ankle-brachial index. Rest pain and tissue loss (ulcer, gangrene) correspond to an ankle-brachial index of 0 to 0.4, the critical limb ischemia band, well below the claudication range.
cites: Arterial Occlusive Diseaase and Aneurysms - Carter.pptx, Slide 42

src.question: A 74-year-old man who smokes wakes most nights with burning pain in his forefoot and toes that eases when he hangs the leg over the bed; he now sleeps in a recliner. Which ankle-brachial index range would be expected?
src.explanation: Correct. Rest pain and tissue loss (ulcer, gangrene) correspond to an ankle-brachial index of 0 to 0.4, the critical limb ischemia band, well below the claudication range.

items.html: Early, stable constriction. Early, hemodynamically stable constriction may get the acute pericarditis medicines (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and colchicine) for longer, 2 to 3 months, with diuretics for fluid overload; edema or late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance suggests reversible inflammation.

src.question: A 45-year-old woman developed early signs of constriction 6 weeks after an episode of acute pericarditis. She is hemodynamically stable, and cardiac magnetic resonance shows pericardial edema with late gadolinium enhancement. Which is the most appropriate next step?
src.key: A longer course of pericarditis drugs
src.explanation: Correct. Early, hemodynamically stable constriction may get the acute pericarditis medicines (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and colchicine) for longer, 2 to 3 months, with diuretics for fluid overload; edema or late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance suggests reversible inflammation.

items.html: Cardioversion follows anticoagulation. In stable atrial fibrillation without a rapid ventricular response, rate control comes first, with anticoagulation guided by stroke risk; elective outpatient cardioversion follows after 21 days of anticoagulation.

src.question: A 66-year-old man with stable atrial fibrillation at 92 asks why the plan is to control his heart rate rather than shock him back into normal rhythm today. Which explanation is most accurate?
src.explanation: Correct. In stable atrial fibrillation without a rapid ventricular response, rate control comes first, with anticoagulation guided by stroke risk; elective outpatient cardioversion follows after 21 days of anticoagulation.

items.html: Pre-excitation and reentry. Pre-excitation (a short PR interval and a delta wave) on an earlier tracing in normal sinus rhythm points to an accessory pathway and the potential for atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia, which runs above 100, usually at 200 to 300, with hidden or retrograde P waves.

src.question: A 26-year-old man has a sudden, regular narrow complex tachycardia at 230 with retrograde (inverted) P waves. An electrocardiogram taken last year in normal sinus rhythm showed a short PR interval and a delta wave (a slurred QRS upstroke). Which diagnosis is most likely?
src.explanation: Correct. Pre-excitation (a short PR interval and a delta wave) on an earlier tracing in normal sinus rhythm points to an accessory pathway and the potential for atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia, which runs above 100, usually at 200 to 300, with hidden or retrograde P waves.

items.section_title: 7.5 · Clinical manifestations and the peripheral signs
items.html: Petechiae. The petechiae of infective endocarditis are minute hemorrhages, and they can be transient, fading rather than persisting.

src.question: How are the petechiae of infective endocarditis described?
src.explanation: Correct. The petechiae of infective endocarditis are minute hemorrhages, and they can be transient, fading rather than persisting.

items.html: Atrioventricular node ischemia. Atrioventricular node ischemia, usually after a myocardial infarction, is a named cause of Mobitz type I block; a block that appears during an infarction fits it.

src.question: A 63-year-old man is admitted with an acute myocardial infarction. He has never had a cardiac procedure and has had no tick bites. On the second hospital day his monitor shows a PR interval that lengthens with each beat until a QRS complex is dropped, in a repeating pattern. Which named cause of this rhythm fits him best?
src.explanation: Correct. Atrioventricular node ischemia, usually after a myocardial infarction, is a named cause of Mobitz type I block; a block that appears during his infarction fits it best.
